objective: Introduce an application orchestration service over immutable application contracts without changing scientific algorithms or model artifacts.

baseline.status: Application data contracts merged; orchestration service is proposed on feat/product-application-services.

correctness.before: No application orchestration boundary existed above the data contracts.
correctness.after: Service validates request identity, operation and source references, then returns a typed immutable result envelope.

reliability.before: Application-level request validation was not centralized.
reliability.after: Focused tests cover invalid requests and result wrapping; CI runs test, package, smoke and security checks.

reproducibility.before: Orchestration contract had no dedicated focused tests.
reproducibility.after: Contract and service behavior are covered by versioned tests and CI evidence tied to the commit.

evidence: CI push run 37858327464 passed including test suite, package build, runtime smoke tests, dependency audit and CI Gate.
Scientific Validation run 37858331211 passed its contract/lifecycle validation job.

root_causes: The initial pull_request CI event failed because the cumulative lifecycle gate requires a machine-readable cycle record whenever source or test files change.
A subsequent push-triggered CI run on the same head commit passed; the missing cycle record still needs to be added to make the PR event pass consistently.

findings: Any PR changing implementation or tests must include a cumulative lifecycle cycle record under configs/process/cycles/.
A successful push CI run does not erase a failed pull_request event; both event paths must be reviewed.

open_blockers: Re-run pull_request checks after adding this cycle record and verify every required check is green before merge.

knowledge_carried_forward: verify all PR event checks before merge
